subject: Region runway, GPU SKU mix & compliance notes for upcoming HorizonAI commit
messages:
From: Carl Fisher <carl@horizonai.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@horizonai.com
Date: Fri, 3 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial capacity ask & compliance checks for HK pilot

Diego —

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Quick summary from our side: HorizonAI expects a 6–9 month pilot beginning late May to validate inference latency for their chat product in APAC. They want a dedicated lane in APAC (Hong Kong pilot region) with predictable burst capacity to handle ~4k qps at 512 tokens/session peak.

Two asks up front:
- Can Redwood propose SKU mixes (H100 vs A100 vs L4) and an estimated runway (nodes committed vs burst) for a 9-month pilot? We need a cost estimate for budgeting.
- Hong Kong has a few data-residency and KMS expectations — we attached the checklist we've received from legal; can you confirm what Redwood can support (bring-your-own-KMS, audit logs retention)?

Appreciate a short plan + any blockers by EOD Tuesday so we can flag to procurement.

—Carl
Director, Platform Engineering
HorizonAI

Attachments: horizon_hk_checklist.pdf (pdf, 145KB)
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Carl Fisher <carl@horizonai.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, mina_haddad@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 3 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial capacity ask & compliance checks for HK pilot

Carl —

Thanks for the clear asks. High-level reply here; internal details and an XLS with scenarios attached.

1) SKU mix recommendation (pilot -> production ramp) - Short pilot (4–9 months): primarily H100 80GB for low latency gen workloads. Use a small percentage (10–20%) of A100 80GB as a failover lane for compatibility and to reduce cost where model distillation/quantized variants can run. Consider L4 for embedding/cheap background jobs but not for peak chat inference.

2) Runway / node sizing (9-month baseline) - Committed baseline: 16 H100 nodes (sustained 1.2k qps steady, region-local KV cache enabled). - Burst lane (reserved but billed differently): +8 burst nodes (H100) available for spiky windows up to 4k qps. - Fallback: cross-region burst to SG/Tokyo or EU if HK capacity constrained; will add cross-region latency (we'll quantify).

3) Compliance / KMS / logging - BYO-KMS via customer-managed keys in the VPC/private deployment is supported for Private customers; hosted offering needs an enterprise private deployment option (we have a standard integration pattern). - Audit logs / retention: we can provide token-level audit logs for the requested 12 months (configurable). We will need a short security questionnaire answered to map certificates and certifiers.

4) Costs - I attached SKU-level cost breakdown (sheet: scenario_A / scenario_B). Rough order: committed baseline + burst reservation for 9 months ~ ballpark $1.2M–$1.6M depending on H100 availability and reserved pricing. Final numbers when procurement confirms tranches.

Next steps I propose: internal alignment (see internal thread below) and then a short 30-min review with procurement + our Solutions Architect next Tue.

Diego
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: horizon_runway_scenario_v2.xlsx; sku-cost-breakdown.csv
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, mina_haddad@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 6 Apr 2027 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: HK pilot SKU mix, thermal & supply constraints (please review)

Team —

Looping you in with Carl's ask and my initial reply (attached). Two operational notes I need your input on before we present to Horizon procurement:

1) Supply & lead times - H100 availability in the APAC region is patchy for Q2–Q3. If we commit 16 baseline + 8 burst H100 nodes for a 9-month pilot, we need to either: (a) guarantee longer lead time (order now, deploy May) or (b) offer a mixed baseline with 6 A100 nodes to cover early weeks while H100 capacity is provisioned. The latter would change performance but keeps the pilot start date.

2) Cooling / power / DC constraints for candidate HK partner (Suzanne at GlobalDataCenters) - They flagged 32A rack power limits and elevated density costs for H100 due to power draw. If we go with full H100 baseline, we might need more racks or move some nodes to SG with cross-region fallback. That will increase inter-region traffic and slightly increase p99 latency.

3) Pricing / commit structure recommendation - Option A (fast start): Mixed baseline (10 H100 + 6 A100) with immediate deploy to meet May start; then migrate to 16H100 over 6 weeks as supply arrives. - Option B (pure H100): Delay start by 4–6 weeks to deploy full H100 fleet (preferred perf-wise).

Please reply with preferred option and any redlines by EOD tomorrow so I can finalize the workbook for procurement.

Diego

Diego / team —

Good notes. Quick decisions / asks from infra & biz dev perspective:

1) Go with Option A (mixed baseline) as a pragmatic compromise so Horizon can start late May. We should make the migration plan explicit: milestone-based swap of 6 A100 -> H100 per fortnight as inventory clears. Include a clause for 'SKU parity' (same performance profile) being the condition for invoice tier change.

2) Rack / power mitigation: ask Suzanne to confirm whether we can secure contiguous racks (2U spacing) or get temporary elevated power allowance for the pilot; offer to colocate burst nodes in SG and provide a failover SLO. I'll draft a short note to Suzanne.

3) Pricing ask to Finance: give me committed baseline price for Option A and the per-month incremental cost for each H100 added post-deploy. We need a transparent transition metric (percent of traffic on H100) to trigger billing change.

4) Compliance: Mina — please confirm earliest we can support BYO-KMS in a Hosted+Private combo (customer-managed keys at region-edge) and whether token-level audit retention for 12 months is on by-default or needs a paid add-on.

I'll prep the note to procurement and copy Diego on the timeline.

Thanks,
Karthik
VP, Sales Engineering
